Bug_Title: "wait(...)" should be used instead of "Thread.sleep(...)" when a lock is held
Bug_Details:
In a multithreaded environment, a thread may need to wait for a particular condition to become true. One way of pausing execution in Java is Thread.sleep(…​) .
If a thread that holds a lock calls Thread.sleep(…​) , no other thread can acquire said lock. This can lead to performance and
scalability issues, in the worst case leading to deadlocks.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using Thread.sleep(...) while holding a lock. This prevents other threads from acquiring the lock, which can lead to performance issues and potential deadlocks.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method on an instance of LockAndSleepExample. The method uses Thread.sleep while holding a lock, which causes the test to fail due to the condition not being met in a timely manner, demonstrating the performance issue caused by not using wait().
